questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the nature and the town itself. Also it was important that the university offered courses that were interesting academically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. The university was very good at providing the necessary resources.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were information meetings that covered everythijng necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Not very easy. But not impossible either. 
My recommendations would be to start looking for housing early (perhaps something like 3 or 4 months before coming), and to be ready to pay a very high rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is what most people do in Boulder, however you should be prepared to pay an expensive rent and to have roommates that are not perfect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is all done on their course website. It is done easily, and for courses that require prerequisites you contact the faculties. They are very responsive and helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university contact was very good at answering questions or directing me to the relevant people within the faculties.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted without any problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read the emails sent to you, and it will go smoothly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the academic level was quite low on all my courses. In hindsight I should have taken MA courses, but it was presented as a solution that CU Boulder did not like much, and it was a bit more labourious to enter the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very much like being back in high school. A lot of class room teaching and many assignments. Not many lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Plasma Physics, Introduction to American Literature by Women, Astrophysics: Stellar and Interstellar, Number Theory: Introduction to Higher Mathematics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Of the four courses I took, Introduction to Plasma Physics was by far the besdt course. The teacher, Michael Litos, did well and the course was well structured.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing was quite a bit more expensive than I expected. I was extremely lucky to find housing at "only" 4300 DKK a month. Everybody else paid way more (up to twice as much). Food was also a bit more expensive than expected. Especially fruits and vegetables cost a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a ton of cool clubs. The university recreation center provided a lot of athletic activities for free such as a gym, clinbing wall, tennis courts, a pool, and many more sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely check out the student societies and clubs. I can recommend the Alpine Club for anyone interested in climbing and the outdoors.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on trips during the weekends were the highlight of my trip. Colorado has so much to offer in terms of nature, and the neighboring states, Utah and Wyoming, are also very beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. It is very much as you would expect from movies and television, but it is till very interesting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the student clubs!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The towns and cities are very car-centric. Not having a car or knowing anyone with a car makes it way more difficult to really enjoy what Colorado has to offer.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendlyness of the americans.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to take MA courses, rent a bike through the university, and start looking for housing early on (try different groups on Facebook).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting local americans and experiencing the american culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not have any great challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
